responses.reason: The table shows account 4200 fell $65,000 and 34.9 percent, not the $6,500 and 3.5 percent this challenge cites, so the conclusion is wrong too.
S1 says the repair program finished June 30 but S10 calls part of it remaining work due in August, so the two sentences cannot both be true.
The table has account 5100 going from $214,000 to $287,800, which is an increase, so S6 saying it declined looks backwards to me.
S9 says the $84,000 covers twelve months to May 2027 but books all of it as June revenue, which does not sound like where it belongs.
S12 already states that professional fees fails the dollar leg of the threshold, so I do not think an engagement letter is needed for something that small.
Inventory shrink only moved $2,500 against a $25,000 threshold, so asking for the cycle count file on a line this size seems like more than is owed.
S5 names the Tri-State depot ramp as the reason for the $372,000 change without a schedule, contract, or rate change behind it anywhere in the memo.
S2 states bad debt increased $42,000 but the table shows account 6400 moving $47,000, and those two figures do not agree with each other.
S8 mentions $19,400 of fuel invoices pushed into July, which is larger than the $5,200 the account shows for the whole month, so June looks light.
Software subscriptions moved only $1,600 on 5.6 percent, which fails both legs of the threshold, so S3 probably should not be a full sentence in this memo.
Warehouse wages moved $72,500, which clears both the dollar and percent threshold, and I cannot find a sentence anywhere that explains what drove it.
Account 4000 rose $372,000 the same month account 4200 fell $65,000, and neither sentence says whether freight billing moved into product revenue.
S11 rounds both months to 24 percent, and if May was actually nearer 25 before rounding, the stable mix and pricing story does not hold up the same way.
S7 blames the $31,200 interest increase on equipment that also sits in depreciation, but account 7000 shows zero variance, so depreciation does not back that up.
